bridges.name: Orientation-Closure Bridge

statement.formal: Stable closure probability depends on coherent orientation structure.

MODEL_A.name: Orientation After Asymmetry
MODEL_A.description: Orientation is induced after asymmetry and does not participate directly in closure generation.

MODEL_B.name: Orientation Participatory
MODEL_B.description: Orientation is an active closure-forming component.

hypotheses.H0: Closure stability is independent of orientation coherence.
hypotheses.H1: Closure stability depends on orientation coherence.

bridges.success_condition: Orientation coherence predicts closure persistence significantly better than random controls.

failure_conditions.minimum: Orientation coherence provides no measurable predictive value.
failure_conditions.strong: Randomized orientation performs as well or better than coherent orientation.

bridges.name: Orientation-Closure Bridge (Consequence Model)

statement.informal: Orientation is a consequence of stable triadic closure.
statement.formal: Coherent orientation is induced by the stabilized triadic closure of distinction-nodes.

bridges.reason_for_rewrite: LFCR_001 demonstrated that orientation coherence does not drive closure stability (Model B falsified). v2 shifts the dependency to Model A where orientation is a signature or secondary stabilizer of already-formed closure.
